claims.claim: The shared guard bounds complete decision enumeration, exact-ref batches, arguments and responses. Native-Git fixtures cover zero/one/32/128, capacity, cold/warm, malformed, duplicate, incomplete and over-capacity cases without skipping mandatory rechecks.

Each decision retains current remote source ref/full SHA binding matched to REVIEW.reviewed_sha. Immutable commit reuse validates type and raw-byte hash, ignores replacement refs, fetches missing exact objects and rejects corrupt or wrong-type objects.
Pre-write rechecks freshly query bound refs, compare the complete decision set and re-observe main. Regressions cover added, deleted, moved and swapped refs with typed fail-closed outcomes.

Eligible historical competing PASS sources retain canonical lineage validation and COMPETING_REVIEWED_SOURCE blocking, without age filtering or winner selection; regressions cover both ref orderings and warm objects.

Publisher APIs, typed outcomes, normal/replay/inclusion/correction/recovery paths, exact reservation ownership, expected-old-main CAS and publication postconditions remain intact. Race regressions assert exact blockers and absence of rejected main writes.

Prior source-bound matched measurements for the unchanged production guard report warm-local remote calls falling from 99 to 5 at 32 decisions and 387 to 7 at 128, both below 25 percent of baseline. The five-pair harness reports identical outcomes, per-category calls, raw elapsed times and inconclusive production timing.

AUTHOR_TASK implementation retains direct-final validation, legacy/ORIGIN_AFFINE distinctions, main/transport checks, audited-handoff rejection, immutable revision replay and reservation/publication compatibility, with focused warm-guard regressions.

The focused native-Git module compares an immutable pre-G1 baseline with the candidate using five repetitions per zero/32/128 cold/warm condition and adversarial regressions. Source APIs and the permitted candidate scope are preserved; this repair changes only the authorized document.

Candidate roadmap root next_items, sole sequence NEXT, active_track and planning_document agree on git-decision-guard-priority-20261022. One conditional residual queue exists; v1.3 remains paused and resumable, preserving historical planning and lineage.

The committed document now uses 'non-overlapping' in the conditional G2 residual-cost description. Both plans retain one G1 TASK, zero-or-one residual G2 TASK without double-counted gains, then explicit Human/Brain return to unfinished L3-05/L3-06/G3/G6/L4 after TASK-397 reconciliation. Brain Sync regressions cover conflicting selectors and transport-only inference.
